title: Docker and the OCI standard: why the specification matters

videos.script: An image built on Ana's laptop runs on a cluster that has never seen Docker. That works because the format is not Docker's any more. It belongs to three open specifications. {{specs}} One says what an image is. One says how a registry hands it out. And one says how a runtime starts a container from it. {{open}} Then you open an image. It turns out to be a few JSON files and a tar archive. Each file is named after the hash of its own bytes. {{hash}} Change one byte, and the name no longer matches. That is what makes a digest trustworthy. {{runc}} And last, you start a container with no Docker at all. A directory, one configuration file, and runc. It prints its own host name and sees itself as process one. Everything Docker does happens around that moment.
